memory_candidates.content: When a bash reason-ladder function computes a boolean signal (e.g. kill -0 result) but only conditionally derives a string reason from it, the signal can get silently discarded in a later fallback branch that re-derives a weaker/wrong conclusion from other fields (e.g. 'pid is numeric' standing in for 'process is alive'). Fix pattern: capture the signal in its own local (pid_dead=false, set true at the point of computation) and consult that local FIRST in every downstream branch, rather than re-testing the original raw fields.

Falsifiability check technique for a bugfix plan: git stash push --keep-index -- <single-file-path> isolates one file's edits from other already-staged/modified files in the working tree. Useful when new test assertions must be proven to fail against pre-fix code, but the test files themselves (which carry the new assertions) must NOT be reverted along with the fix — only the fix file. Restore with git stash pop.

A plan's 'Scope Hypothesis' re-sweep (grep for the pattern being fixed across the whole repo, not just the declared file list) can surface implicit membership-list defects beyond the explicitly declared files -- e.g. a code comment enumerating allowed values without the newly-added one. Pre-authorizing 'any additional site found is an in-scope incidental edit, recorded in the summary' in the plan avoids a scope-creep debate mid-implementation while still requiring documentation.
